problem.heading: Relevant tenders get lost in the noise
problem.body: Belgium's public tender feed publishes thousands of notices a year, in four languages, across every sector. Scanning it by hand for the handful that fit your business costs hours — and in testing, about a third of an unfiltered feed turned out to be notices for contracts that were already awarded. Miss the right one, or waste time screening the wrong ones, and you bid on less than you could.

items.question: What is TenderProc, exactly?
items.answer: TenderProc is an AI-assisted platform for finding and preparing bids on Belgian public tenders. It matches new tenders to your business, screens out noise (like already-awarded notices), and helps you qualify and prepare a bid — all in one workflow.

items.question: How does the AI matching work?
items.answer: Every new tender gets a match score out of 100 against your company profile (sectors, size, description) — so you see what's actually worth your time first.

items.question: Do I need experience with public tenders to use this?
items.answer: No — TenderProc is built to make Belgian public procurement approachable even if you've never bid before. You set up a company profile, and the platform handles screening, requirement extraction, and eligibility checks.

items.question: Which regions/sectors are covered?
items.answer: Belgian public tenders nationwide, across sectors from construction and IT to healthcare, catering, and consulting. Above the EU publication threshold, we cover all of Belgium via the EU's TED database and Belgium's BOSA e-Notification platform. Below that threshold, coverage comes from regional council-decision data and currently varies by region — strongest in Wallonia, partial in Flanders, not yet available for Brussels. We're actively expanding this.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: Free, Pro (€49/month), and Premium (€79/month) — see the Pricing page for what's included in each.

items.question: Is there a free trial?
items.answer: There's no time-limited trial, but the Free plan itself never expires and needs no card — you can try tender discovery for one sector at no cost before upgrading.

items.question: Can I cancel anytime?
items.answer: Yes — cancel anytime from the Billing page. Cancelling stops future renewals; you keep paid-tier access until your current period ends and aren't charged again after that.

items.question: Is my company data secure/GDPR-compliant?
items.answer: Yes — TenderProc is GDPR-compliant by design (documented legal basis for every use of your data, EU data-subject rights honored), data in transit is encrypted (HTTPS), and access is scoped to your own account. Full details are in our Privacy Notice.

items.question: How often are new tenders added?
items.answer: Tenders are pulled live from the EU's official TED database as they're published — not on a batch delay — plus a daily digest email flags anything new in your sectors.

items.question: Can I get help preparing my actual bid, or just find opportunities?
items.answer: Both — beyond discovery, Pro includes AI-assisted bid preparation: upload a tender PDF and TenderProc extracts requirements, scores your fit with a Bid/No-Bid recommendation, and drafts a response grounded in your own company evidence.

items.question: What languages does the platform support?
items.answer: The app itself is available in English, Dutch, French, and German, and tender notices published in other languages can be AI-translated for you.

items.question: What happens if I miss a deadline notification?
items.answer: There isn't a dedicated deadline-reminder feature yet — each tender's deadline is shown right on its card, and once you add it to your Workflow board you can track it there through review, drafting and submission, so nothing you're actively pursuing gets lost.

Privacy.title: Privacy Notice
Privacy.intro: This notice explains what personal data TenderProc collects, why, and what rights you have over it under the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and Belgian data protection law. It applies to visitors of our website and users of the TenderProc app.

s1.h: 1. Who is responsible for your data
s1.p1: The data controller is {entityName}, commercial registration / tax number {companyNumber}. For any question about this notice or to exercise your rights, contact us at {emailAddress}.
s1.p2: We’re established outside the European Union but offer the Service to businesses in Belgium and the EU, so this notice, and GDPR itself, still applies to how we handle your data (GDPR Art. 3(2)).

s2.p1: Account data: your email address and password (stored hashed by our authentication provider, Supabase — we never see the plaintext password).
s2.p2: Company profile: company name, address, size, sectors, description, website, employee count, regions served and languages served — collected at signup and editable on your Company page.
s2.p3: Company knowledge base: the services you offer, certifications, past references (which may include contract values), and supporting documents you upload. This is used to generate match scores and eligibility checks, and — only where you choose to — as source material for AI-drafted bid responses.
s2.p4: Tenders and bids: tenders you upload or track, the requirements and award criteria we extract from them, your bid workspace data (status, checklists, uploaded bid documents, AI-drafted response text), and — if you record it — the outcome of a bid, which may include competitively sensitive figures like winning price or your own score.
s2.p5: Technical data: standard request data (IP address, browser user-agent) generated by using a web app, session cookies used to keep you signed in, and a cookie storing your language preference. We don’t run third-party advertising or analytics trackers.

s3.h: 3. Why we process it, and on what legal basis
s3.li1: Providing the Service — creating your account, matching tenders to your profile, running eligibility checks, generating draft bid responses, and running your bid workspace. Legal basis: performance of our contract with you (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).
s3.li2: Billing — processing your subscription via Paddle, and keeping records required for accounting and tax law. Legal basis: contract performance and legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(b) and (c) GDPR).
s3.li3: Service notifications — sending the tender digest email for sectors you’ve selected. Legal basis: legitimate interest in operating the feature you configured (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR); you can turn this off in your preferences at any time.
s3.li4: Security and abuse prevention — protecting accounts and the Service from unauthorized access. Legal basis: legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
s3.li5: Legal compliance — responding to lawful requests, tax and accounting record-keeping. Legal basis: legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR).
s3.p1: AI-assisted outputs (match scores, eligibility checks, drafted text) are generated to help you, not to make decisions about you — TenderProc doesn’t use automated processing to make decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects concerning you within the meaning of Art. 22 GDPR. A human — you — always reviews and decides before anything is submitted to a contracting authority.

s4.intro: We share personal data with the following processors, each bound by a data processing agreement, and only to the extent needed to provide the Service:
s4.li1: Supabase — hosts our database, authentication and file storage. Project region: {supabaseRegion}.
s4.li2: Anthropic — processes tender and company text you submit to generate match scores, eligibility checks, and draft bid responses. Anthropic is based in the United States; transfers are covered by Standard Contractual Clauses or an equivalent safeguard.
s4.li3: Resend — delivers the tender-digest email and other transactional emails.
s4.li4: Paddle — processes payments and acts as Merchant of Record for paid subscriptions; Paddle receives the billing details needed to process your payment (Paddle, not us, holds your card details).
s4.p1: Tender and award data flowing the other way — from the EU’s TED database and Belgium’s e-Procurement/BOSA platform into TenderProc — is public procurement data, not your personal data; we don’t send your data to these sources.
s4.p2: We don’t sell personal data, and we don’t share it with third parties for their own marketing purposes.

s5.p1: Your data leaves the EU/EEA in more than one way here, and we want to be direct about that rather than bury it: our database and file storage (Supabase) are hosted in {supabaseRegion}, our AI processing provider (Anthropic) is based in the United States, and {entityName} itself, as controller, is established outside the EU/EEA. For each of these transfers, we rely on the European Commission’s Standard Contractual Clauses or another lawful transfer mechanism recognized under GDPR Chapter V to protect your data. You can ask us for a copy of the relevant safeguard by contacting us at <email>{emailAddress}</email>.

s6.p1: We keep your account and workspace data for as long as your account is active. If you delete your account, we delete or anonymize your personal data within a reasonable period, except data we’re required to keep for longer — for example, billing and invoice records, which we retain for the period required by Belgian accounting and tax law.

s7.intro: Under GDPR, you have the right to:
s7.li1: Access the personal data we hold about you;
s7.li3: Ask us to delete your data (subject to our legal retention obligations, e.g. for invoices);
s7.li4: Restrict or object to certain processing;
s7.li5: Receive your data in a portable format;
s7.li6: Withdraw consent at any time, where processing is based on consent;
s7.li7: Lodge a complaint with the Belgian Data Protection Authority (Gegevensbeschermingsautoriteit / Autorité de protection des données) or your own EU supervisory authority.
s7.p1: To exercise any of these rights, contact us at <email>{emailAddress}</email>. We may need to verify your identity before acting on a request.

s8.p1: We use only strictly necessary cookies: one to keep you signed in (set by Supabase authentication) and one to remember your language preference. We don’t use advertising or third-party analytics cookies. Because these cookies are strictly necessary for the Service to function, we don’t show a cookie consent banner for them.

s9.p1: Data in transit is encrypted (HTTPS). Access to your data within the Service is scoped to your own account through row-level security enforced at the database layer — by default, no other customer’s account can query your data. Access by TenderProc staff is limited to what’s needed for support and operating the Service.

s10.p1: TenderProc is a business-to-business service and isn’t directed at, or knowingly used by, children.

s11.p1: We may update this notice from time to time. If a change is material, we’ll make reasonable efforts to notify you before it takes effect.

s1.p1: The Free plan is never billed. Pro and Premium are monthly subscriptions, charged in advance, and processed by Paddle, our payment provider, who acts as the Merchant of Record for these purchases — Paddle is the seller of record on your receipt and the party that actually processes the charge.

s2.p1: We don’t offer automatic refunds. Refund requests are reviewed case by case — email us at {emailAddress} with your account email and the reason for the request, and we’ll review it and get back to you. We’re generally receptive to requests raised promptly (for example, shortly after an unwanted renewal, or where the Service genuinely didn’t work for you), and we always correct our own mistakes — see below.

s3.li1: Duplicate charges for the same billing period;
s3.li2: Charges caused by a verified technical error on our side;
s3.li3: Any charge that shouldn’t have happened at all — for example, billing after you’d already cancelled.

s4.p1: You can cancel a subscription anytime from the Billing page in the app. Cancelling stops future renewals — your current paid period isn’t refunded, but you keep paid-tier access until it ends, and you’re not charged again after that.

s5.h: 5. How an approved refund is paid
s5.p1: Approved refunds are processed by Paddle back to your original payment method. Depending on your bank or card provider, it can take a few business days for the refund to appear on your statement.

s6.p1: If something’s wrong with a charge, please contact us first — most issues are resolved faster directly than through a chargeback, and a chargeback can result in your account being suspended while it’s investigated.

s7.p1: Nothing in this policy limits any non-waivable right you have under applicable consumer protection law, including any statutory right of withdrawal for the purchase of digital services that Paddle’s checkout process asks you to acknowledge at the point of purchase.

s8.p1: Refund requests and questions about this policy: <email>{emailAddress}</email>.
